title: Karl Organizing: Financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Financial Transparency] Can you explain: how do we handle the money we raise together?

Here's how it works: Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, surveillance Awareness] How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, surveillance Awareness] What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

Here's how it works: A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: Using Voter Files
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Using Voter Files] Can you explain: do we really need expensive voter data software?

Here's how it works: Data is just a map, but you're the one who has to walk the path. Use the basic public records to find out who hasn't been talked to in years—the renters, the young people, and the marginalized who the big parties ignore. Don't get bogged down in spreadsheets; use the information to target the doors where a conversation will have the most impact. Our strategy is to expand the electorate by engaging the people the system has abandoned.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] Can you explain: how do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Let me break it down: Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails.

title: Karl Organizing: Corporate Landlords
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Corporate Landlords] We rent from a massive corporation based in another state. How do we fight someone we can't see?

Every corporation has a face and an address. Find out who the CEO is, where they live, and who their investors are. Don't just picket the local leasing office; take the fight to their corporate headquarters or the fancy gala they're attending. Use the internet to find other buildings they own and link up with those tenants to create a multi-city front that hits their stock price.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: elderly Care] Give me the short version: How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?

Here's how it works: Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, encrypted Messaging] What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: skillshare Organization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: skillshare Organization] Give me the short version: I want to teach people how to fix bikes, but I've never organized a workshop before.

Look, Grab your tools, find a public park or a community center, and put up some flyers with a clear time and date. Keep it hands-on and skip the long lectures—people learn best by doing, not by listening to us talk. Make sure the space is accessible to everyone and encourage those who learn quickly to start helping the newcomers. We're breaking the monopoly on knowledge that the bosses use to keep us dependent and helpless.

title: Karl Organizing: Signal Apps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signal Apps] How should we communicate during the actual protest?

Use Signal with disappearing messages set to one hour or less to keep your plans off the state's servers. Avoid using voice calls on the open airwaves because the cops have 'stingrays' that can intercept your location and your data. Keep the group chats focused on logistics—water, police movement, and route changes—and save the theory for the post-protest debrief. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Burnout] I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?

You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Sourcing] We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?

Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building Trust] A friend asked me: 'How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant rights research
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant rights research] How do I learn my tenant rights?

Here's how it works: Start with your city's tenant union or legal aid — they have know-your-rights guides for your specific laws. Read your lease carefully; landlords count on you not reading it. Document every maintenance request in writing. Know your state's rules on security deposits, notice periods, and retaliation. Knowledge is leverage.

title: Karl Organizing: Grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grant Alternatives] Can you explain: foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Let me break it down: Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights] What's the most important thing to know about my rights?

Your most important right is the right to remain silent, but remember that the law is often whatever the guy with the badge and the gun says it is in the moment. Always film the police from a safe distance to document their behavior, as that footage is often our only shield in court. Knowledge is power, so host a 'Know Your Rights' training for the whole crew before you ever step foot on the pavement. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Lines] Should we try to push through the police line?

Only if that's the collective plan and everyone is prepared for the inevitable escalation. Pushing a line is often seen as assault, so if you're not looking for a felony, keep a safe distance and hold your ground. We win by being smarter and more organized than the goons in riot gear, not just by brute force.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Interactions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Interactions] What do I say if a cop tries to talk to me?

The only thing you say to a cop is 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I do not consent to a search.' They aren't your friends, and they aren't there to keep you safe; they are there to protect the property of the rich. Keep your hands visible, stay calm, and don't give them a single shred of information they can use to hurt our movement later. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: ICE watch
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[ICE watch] What do I do if I see ICE in my neighborhood?

Verify first — don't spread panic over a rumor. If confirmed, alert the rapid response network immediately. Film from a distance. Remind neighbors of their rights: don't open the door, don't sign anything, ask for a judicial warrant. Connect families with immigration lawyers. Speed and calm save people.

title: Karl Organizing: After the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[After the Win] A friend asked me: 'What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?' What do I tell them?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: avoiding Burnout] Give me the short version: I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?

Let me break it down: You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: House Parties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[House Parties] How do we make a house party fundraiser actually successful?

Keep the speeches short and the energy high. You want people to feel the heat of the movement, not sit through a boring lecture. Have a clear, bold 'ask' halfway through the night, pass a physical bucket, and make sure everyone knows exactly what fight that money is going toward before the music starts back up. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Long-term Planning] Can you explain: how do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Let me break it down: Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] How do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] Can you explain: how do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Look, Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sliding Scales] How do we implement a sliding scale for events?

Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?

Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, right to Remain Silent
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, right to Remain Silent] What should I say if a cop starts questioning me at a rally?

Look, You say absolutely nothing except 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I want a lawyer.' These pigs aren't looking for the truth; they're looking for a reason to put a comrade in a cage. Shut your mouth, stay firm, and don't let their friendly routine trick you into betraying the movement. Silence is your best weapon in the back of a squad car.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: rapid Response Setup] Give me the short version: How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?

Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests.

title: Karl Organizing: The supermajority
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The supermajority] We have 51% of people signed up. Can we file for an election now?

Here's the thing: If you file with 51%, the boss will peel off enough people with lies and threats to crush you by election day. You don't move until you have 70% or 80%. You need a buffer for the people who will get scared and drop out under pressure. Aim for a supermajority so that when the boss starts the psychological warfare, your foundation stays rock solid.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, metadata Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, metadata Awareness] What is 'scrubbing' and how do I do it?

Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM. Now go organize.
